title: Add benchmark-lab mixed-workload runners and reporting pipeline (v45)
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: broaden the benchmark-lab coverage to include mixed and multi-variant workload patterns seen in production (chat + embeddings + reranking bursts) and provide end-to-end reporting for profiling baselines. Changes in this PR: 1) new representative workload runners (mixed_workload_runner.py) that orchestrate conversational generation, embedding trips, and reranking stages with configurable variant mixes and token/latency distributions; 2) profiling baselines for v45 (profiling/baselines/v45.yaml) capturing cold-start, steady-state, and burst scenarios and the scripts to collect KV/cache metrics; 3) reporting pipeline (ci/pipelines/benchmark-reporting-v45.yaml) to aggregate run results, push summaries to BigQuery, and publish perf dashboards; 4) small SDK helpers (redwood-sdk-python/bench/utils.py) for deterministic request replay and deterministic seeding across workers; 5) docs (redwood-docs/benchmark-lab/mixed-workloads.md) with runbook and recommended model/quantization matrices; 6) CI: added e2e-bench-run job and testdata fixtures. Implementation notes: runners use existing runner abstraction and add a new MixedWorkloadProfile that accepts a variant map and concurrency schedule; KV cache warmup is simulated using warmup_requests() which reuses the existing cache API; reporting pipeline normalizes token-level latencies and computes P50/P90/P99 and cost-per-1k-tokens. Backwards compatibility: runners are additive and opt-in via config; reporting uses a new table (bench_v45) in BigQuery but falls back to bench_latest if unavailable. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for runner orchestration - [x] integration e2e bench run - [x] docs and runbook - [x] update Linear links and release notes Related: Linear ENG-3721, ENG-3789.
